title: "Reservoir Sampling"

## What is the real challenge?

**LeetCode 382 — Linked List Random Node.** Maintain a uniform sample from a stream without knowing its final size.

This LeetCode label may describe a **problem domain, engineering interface or probabilistic method** rather than a universally named algorithm. The first step is to state which contract is required.

## The tempting solution

Load the whole unknown-length stream into memory before selecting one uniformly random element.

## The idea worth remembering

Maintain one selected item. At the i-th arrival, replace the current sample with probability 1/i. Surprisingly, every earlier item retains equal probability after the final arrival.

## One mathematical expression — with every symbol explained

$$
P(\text{item }j\text{ survives after }n)=\frac1n
$$

**Every symbol means:** n is total number of observed items; j is any particular item's arrival index, between 1 and n; P is the probability over the sampler's random choices.

**Numerical substitution:** For three items A,B,C: A is initially selected with probability 1. It survives B with probability (1−1/2)=1/2 and C with probability (1−1/3)=2/3. Multiply: 1×1/2×2/3=1/3. B is selected with 1/2 then survives C with 2/3, also 1/3. C enters with 1/3.

The substituted numbers are not decoration: if the example disagrees with the formula, the statement or its assumptions must be corrected before code is written.

## Why the method is justified

Induction: before arrival i, earlier item j has probability 1/(i−1); it survives the i-th replacement with probability (i−1)/i, giving 1/i. New item i is selected with 1/i.

**Complexity or resource cost:** O(n) total processing and O(1) memory for one sample; selecting k samples needs O(k) memory.

## Executable example

The following small example can be run directly in its own environment:

~~~js
let chosen=null;
for(let i=1;i<=3;i++) {
  if(Math.random() < 1/i) chosen=['A','B','C'][i-1];
}
console.log(chosen); // each item has probability 1/3
~~~

Run the JavaScript with Node.js; it illustrates the precise toy case from the formula.

## Which assumption makes it fail?

Selecting each new item with a fixed probability such as 1/2 is biased toward later arrivals. Reservoir sampling assumes the stream sampling policy and replacement random numbers meet its conditions.

For this topic, distinguish an **exact probability or invariant** from a single random observation or a successful local test. A test samples executions; it is not a proof that all executions behave correctly.
